function: system: OTA federated learning (area 7) over single-antenna clients and a single-antenna access point with scalar fading per client, no RIS; p. 4, eq. (6); p. 5.
notes: PDF matches the DOI: p. 1 holds the title 'Adaptive Federated Learning Over the Air' and 'Digital Object Identifier 10.1109/TSP.2025.3585002'. Codes 1-5 do not apply: a research article that proposes and evaluates ADOTA-FL (AdaGrad-OTA and Adam-OTA server updates); OTA FL passes no_learning; the aggregation is analog over the air, not digital (p. 4: 'This method employs A-OTA computations in the global gradient aggregation stage'), so its problem falls in area 7. Code 6 applies: each client and the access point have one antenna and there is no RIS. p. 4: 'we are able to write the real-valued signal that the access point receives as follows', eq. (6) y(s) = sum_n hn,t Pn xtn(s) + xi(s); p. 5: 'where hn,t is the channel fading experienced by client n' (a scalar, also in eq. (7) and Algorithm 1); Fig. 1 (p. 4) draws a single-antenna access point; p. 8: 'we employ the Rayleigh fading to model the channel gain'. Multiple antennas and beamforming appear only in the related work (p. 3: 'via the use of multiple antennae'), and the work is neither OTFS nor NTN. Quantitative results exist (test accuracy and training loss, pp. 8-11), so code 7 would not apply.
